notes_for_owner: UNTESTED: formDAM had no build workflow, so no earlier run backs this entry. './formDAM desktop build' only execs ./build_app (which takes no --config), and the launcher has no install or install-desktop, so this entry runs build_app directly (macOS and Linux) and build_app.bat (Windows); they call setup/build_macos_app, setup/build_linux_app and setup/build_windows_app.bat. Version: tauri.conf.json's version is the path '../frontend/package.json' (Tauri reads the version from there), so the registry reads frontend/package.json (src-tauri/Cargo.toml carries the same version, and release commits bump those two, not tauri.conf.json). Bundles land in src-tauri/target on Linux and Windows but in src-tauri/target.nosync on macOS (setup/build_macos_app hardcodes CARGO_TARGET_DIR), where setup/package_dmg writes formDAM_v<version>.dmg straight into release/bundle; the artifact globs name those paths. Linux builds the deb only (setup/build_linux_app reads BUNDLES, default deb), Windows nsis and msi. The build downloads about a dozen ONNX models from github.com and huggingface.co with sha256 checks, and on macOS runs 'cargo install tauri-cli' if cargo-tauri is missing (slow). macOS signing (formDAM 1.28.3): the identity comes from APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY (formcompiler's build keychain holds it), else the keychain; setup/build_macos_app signs every Mach-O in the engine with it, hardened runtime, a timestamp and src-tauri/Entitlements.plist, and setup/package_dmg keeps Tauri's Developer ID signature instead of re-signing, re-signing w/o --deep only if its icon repair changed the bundle. formcompiler then signs and notarizes the dmg in src-tauri/target.nosync. formcompiler's --config is not passed (no updater). Catalog: identifier is ai.nodemode.dam (tauri.conf.json); products.json says dev.formai.formdam. products.json and the repo's LICENSE say GPL-3.0-only.
